open_points.subject: Customer erasure, revision and last-changed instant
open_points.text: An erasure is not one of them: it keeps no revision (rule 1).
open_points.question: Must an accepted Customer erasure move the last-changed instant and therefore its paired revision, as State 1 says, or must it leave no revision and not count as moving the last-changed instant, as A04 Required test 11 says?
options: Erasure moves both last-changed instant and revision before or despite erasure.
Erasure removes the revision and last-changed instant without moving either; only the erased mark receives its instant.
Erasure removes the revision but replaces or moves the last-changed instant, making the pair exception explicit.
open_points.default_guess: Treat erasure as removing the revision and last-changed instant, write only the erased mark's instant, and correct the State 1 statement that Customer erasure moves the last-changed instant.

witness.initial: A Customer has revision 7, a last-changed instant, contact data, and no erased mark.
events: The owner submits an otherwise valid erasure against revision 7.
outcomes: State 1 requires erasure to move the Customer's last-changed instant; because revision and last-changed instant move exactly together, its revision must also move.
A04 requires the erased Customer to keep no revision and says erasure is not an action that moves its last-changed instant.
witness.observer: The invariant check inspecting the resulting Customer state sees that no result can satisfy both obligations.

open_points.subject: clock reading for revision-moving actions
open_points.text: sets its last-changed instant to the current instant
open_points.question: At what semantic point is the UTC wall-clock instant read, how many readings does one accepted operation take, and must every instant written by that operation—such as last-changed, archived or ended marks, and its audit entry—be identical?
options: Take one UTC wall-clock reading per operation after its checks and share it across every value the operation writes.
Take a separate UTC wall-clock reading for each timestamp field written by the operation.
Take one reading for the changed record but allow separate readings for related marks and the audit entry.
open_points.default_guess: Take one UTC wall-clock reading after all checks succeed and use it for every timestamp written atomically by that operation.

witness.initial: A valid correction begins while a controllable UTC clock reads T0; its record and audit entry will both receive instants.
events: The test clock advances to T1 before the record is written and to T2 before the audit entry is written.
outcomes: With one operation reading, the record and audit entry both carry the same chosen instant.
With separate readings, the record and audit entry may carry T1 and T2.
witness.observer: The owner comparing the corrected record with its audit entry, and the required test using a controllable clock, sees the difference.
